patches.value: AnalyticNotation fixes the following typed conventions, with each function, space, point and measure supplied by its own statement or local scope. D and fderiv denote the Fréchet derivative over the field specified at each use, defaulting to ℝ; deriv is the corresponding one-variable derivative. The total derivative operators return zero when a derivative does not exist. HasDerivAt relates a one-variable function, its derivative value and its basepoint. ContDiffOn and ContDiffAt express the indicated C-order regularity on a set or at a point; ∞ means all finite orders and ω means analytic. minSmoothness at order 2 is 2 for an RCLike normed field and ω otherwise; IsSymmSndFDerivAt means that the second Fréchet derivative at the specified point is symmetric in its two direction arguments. 𝓝 denotes the neighborhood filter. The support of a function is the set where its value is nonzero, tsupport is the closure of that set, and HasCompactSupport means this closure is compact. ContinuousOn means continuity relative to the indicated set. AEStronglyMeasurable means agreement almost everywhere with a strongly measurable function. Integrable means ae strong measurability and finite integral of the norm; IntegrableOn means integrability with respect to the restriction of the specified measure to the specified set. The Bochner integral uses the total library convention; for real integrable functions it is the ordinary finite Lebesgue integral. A set indicator equals its function on that set and zero off it. An ae assertion holds outside a null set for the indicated measure. The extended norm on an ESeminormedAddMonoid is denoted by ‖·‖ₑ; real numbers have finite extended norm. Standard structure names retain their usual mathematical meanings: OpensMeasurableSpace says that open sets are measurable, BorelSpace identifies the measurable structure with the Borel structure, IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts says compact sets have finite measure, and IsAddHaarMeasure means an additive Haar measure. These conventions define notation and assert no application theorem.

patches.old: Induction on the positive order now gives all iterated positive-order Fréchet derivatives zero on O: the first-order case is established; if the order-ℓ derivative map is zero throughout O, each point has a neighborhood on which that map is the constant zero, so M007 makes its next derivative zero there. The same chain-rule directional evaluations as in N001 identify V,A,Psp,Ssp,W with evaluations of the first two derivatives.
patches.new: Induction on the positive derivative order now gives every such derivative zero on O. The first-order case is established. For the step fix an arbitrary positive natural order ell and temporarily assume L1: the order-ell derivative map is zero throughout O. Then each point has a neighborhood on which that map is the constant zero, so M007 makes its next derivative zero there. Discharge L1 to obtain the induction step; natural induction gives all positive orders. Restricting the locally constant map and its derivative maps along the affine time and spatial sections, the ordinary chain rule identifies V,A,Psp,Ssp,W with the corresponding directional evaluations of the first two derivatives; their component section derivatives are the actual ones asserted in N001.
